### Version

1.48.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone my repo at https://github.com/halljus/playwright-1.48.0-repro
2. npm install
3. npx playwright install
4. npm run dev
5. Browse to http://localhost:5173

Observe in the server console that the ~bundler~ compiler (esbuild) cannot resolve `chromium-bidi`.


### Expected behavior

It should just work (either by not requiring a devDependencies library, promoting it to dependencies, or updating documentation with further instructions).

**This error does not occur in playwright v1.47.2, the latest version prior to v1.48.0.**

### Actual behavior

import fs from 'node:fs';
import * as esbuild from 'esbuild';

// Only create source maps for our code. See https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/41541#issuecomment-1457485140
const excludeVendorFromSourceMapPlugin = {
  name: 'excludeVendorFromSourceMapPlugin',
  setup(build) {
    const emptySourceMapAsBase64 = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ version: 3, sources: [''], mappings: 'A' })).toString(
      'base64'
    );
    build.onLoad({ filter: /node_modules.+\.(js|ts)$/ }, (args) => {
      return {
        contents: `${fs.readFileSync(args.path, 'utf8')}\n//# sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64,${emptySourceMapAsBase64}`,
        loader: 'default'
      };
    });
  }
};

console.log('Bundling code');

await esbuild.build({
  logLevel: 'info',
  plugins: [excludeVendorFromSourceMapPlugin],
  external: [
    './chromium/appIcon.png',
    './loader',
    // see https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33031#issuecomment-2404366111
    'chromium-bidi'
  ],
  entryPoints: ['./src/index.ts'],
  bundle: true,
  sourcemap: 'linked',
  sourcesContent: false, // omit the original source code. We only need sensible stack traces. See https://esbuild.github.io/api/#sources-content

  outfile: './dist/index.cjs'
});

I was also experiencing this issue, but have since fixed it without changing vite config or downgrading that package (using 1.56.1). 

The root of the problem was that an import statement was causing vite to detect `playwright` (and eventually `playwright-core`) , which in our environment was causing vite to attempt to bundle them in advance. The issue with pre-bundling these dependencies is that the runtime dependency for `chromium-bidi`  looks on disk _immediately_ for that package, in its own (myPackage's) dependencies. Because we are using `pnpm` and we don't have `chromium-bidi` declared as a dependency, vite can't find it.


To show the problem more directly...
```typescript
// myPackage/tests/steps.ts or some other custom playwright testing file
import { createBdd } from 'playwright'

interface Foo {
  bar: string
}
```
If you then import that interface elsewhere, into a file that vite wants to build, i.e.
```vue
// myPackage/someFile.vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { Foo } from './tests/steps.ts' // Vite will go to the steps file, see the import from playwright at the top, and try to pre-bundle it.
 ...
</script>
```

The solution for us was to move an interface which was causing vite to see imports from playwright. I would imagine the same would apply to any other import statement which ultimately causes vite to detect playwright. In the above example, moving the `Foo` interface from the `steps.ts` file into say `myPackage/types.ts`, and then importing it from that `types.ts` into your `steps.ts` file would not trigger vite to see playwright.
